The periodic acid-Schiff staining showed moderate to diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma ( Figure 1A ), and the periodic acid silver methenamine staining and Masson’s staining showed severe diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma ( Figure 1B ). It was accompanied by diffuse thickening of the basement membrane, small eosinophilic deposits in the subendothelial segment, and microangioma-like expansion of segmental capillary loops.

clinician.trajectory_summary: Initial presentation with intermittent facial and bilateral lower extremity edema and nephrotic range proteinuria (5.54 g/24 h) in a patient with long-standing diabetes, hypertension, and coronary heart disease. Renal biopsy revealed moderate to severe diffuse mesangial cell and stroma proliferation with basement membrane thickening and eosinophilic deposits. Immunofluorescence showed IgA and C3 positivity. Formal pathology classification confirmed mild to moderate mesangial proliferative IgAN (Type IIa). Treatment with methylprednisolone and prophylactic isoniazid for three months partially relieved nephrotic syndrome.
